script.opening_words:
It's 11:00 p.m. You're lying in bed
doing mental math that isn't working
out. You got the degree, you got the
job, you got the promotion, and yet here
you are quietly panicking about whether
the car payment and the electric bill
can both clear this week without you
having to do the embarrassing shuffle
between accounts. Again, that's not a
you problem, that's a trap problem.
Here's what nobody tells you, the middle
class doesn't go broke from one
catastrophic decision. It goes broke
from 20 comp
script.ending_words:
heir lifestyle
could absorb the income. They didn't
need to keep up with anyone because they
were too busy actually building
something. From the outside at 35, they
looked like they hadn't figured out how
to enjoy their money yet. From the
inside at 55, they looked like people
with options. And options, the ability
to choose your work, your time, your
life, are what money is actually for.
You don't have to fix all of this this
week. Pick the trap that stung the most
when you read it, the one where you
thought, "Okay, that one's me." Start
there. That's where your version of this
story changes.
